definition: Re-ordering candidate passages retrieved for a query using a more expensive, more accurate model than the first-stage retriever.
details: Re-ordering candidate passages retrieved for a query using a more expensive, more accurate model than the first-stage retriever. Cross-encoders and listwise LLM rerankers are common choices in RAG and search pipelines.

explainer.lead: Passage re-ranking re-orders the candidate passages returned by a first-stage retriever using a slower, more accurate model. It matters because it sharply improves the passage order that reaches a reader or an LLM, at an affordable cost on a short candidate list.

tiers.eli5: A fast librarian grabs a rough pile of possibly relevant books; a careful expert then reads them and puts the best ones on top.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers retrieve a few dozen to a few hundred candidates cheaply, then rerank with a cross-encoder or a listwise LLM reranker. The pitfall is latency and cost: reranking many candidates is expensive, and a good passage dropped by the first stage can never be recovered.
tiers.paperLevel: Given query q and candidate set C from the first stage, produce an ordering scored by a stronger relevance model; common choices are cross-encoders scoring (q, passage) jointly or listwise LLM rerankers. Quality is bounded by the recall of the initial retrieval.

explainer.example: A retriever returns 100 passages for a question; a cross-encoder scores each query-passage pair and the top 5 are passed to the answer generator.
